messages:
Sophia: Quick check — finished initial quant bring-up for Shuttle13B (INT6 + INT8). Need a short cost-vs-quality scorecard for GTN by EOD. Key metrics: p95 latency, rel unit cost, and quality delta on our product slices.

Benchbot: Run complete — 1,260 evals across longform/qa/summary slices. Artifacts: https://redwood.internal/bench/shuttle13b/6267890123 :white_check_mark:

Leo: can you drop the raw numbers here? product wants to see whether INT8 meets the <1% quality-loss bar.

Mira: quick highlights from the eval CSV: INT8 looks promising. Perf on prod GPU: INT8 ~1.25x vs FP16, INT6 ~1.8x. Quality deltas (aggregated): INT8: -0.9% nDCG_long, -0.4% ROUGE; INT6: -2.3% nDCG_long, -1.1% ROUGE. (slices = longform/qa/recap)

Jules: @Mira that nDCG_long number — is that on GTN's high-attention slice or overall? product cares about the high-attention subset.

Mira: it's overall. On high-attention slice INT8 is -1.1% (fewer samples), INT6 is -3.6%.

Sophia: short table (relative baseline = FP16):
```
variant | rel_cost | p95_latency | delta_nDCG_long | delta_ROUGE_avg
FP16    | 1.00     | 210ms       | 0.0%            | 0.0%
INT8    | 0.78     | 170ms       | -0.9%           | -0.4%
INT6    | 0.47     | 120ms       | -2.3%           | -1.1%
```

Raj: infra note: INT6 requires the new aten kernel and a small runtime build. Also observed slower KV-cache warmstart on cold hosts — recommend warmup=40 for INT6.

Leo: product-level recommendation attempt: INT8 -> roll to 30% traffic with strict monitoring gates (nDCG, ROUGE, hallucination-rate). If stable 48h -> increase to 60%. INT6 -> keep as experimental flag for narrow slices only.

Mira: add fallback policy: if p95 latency > 250ms OR nDCG drop > 1.0% on any product slice -> automatic route to FP16.

Jules: thats reasonable. Need unit-econ numbers for the GTN one-pager: tokens per request ~150 on avg, can you convert rel_cost to $/1k requests?

Sophia: quick calc (relative numbers only): avg tokens = 150. Normalize FP16 = $1.00 per 1k reqs. Then INT8 ~ $0.78 /1k, INT6 ~ $0.47 /1k. So INT8 ≈ 22% savings, INT6 ≈ 53% savings vs FP16.

Benchbot: full CSV + diff scripts posted in artifacts link above (includes per-slice breakdown and raw logs).

Mira: suggested one-line scorecard for GTN: "INT8: Recommended — ~22% unit-cost savings with <1% quality loss on primary slices; INT6: Experimental — ~53% cost savings but >2% regression on longform/high-attention slices."

Jules: Product ok w/ that messaging for internal GTN comms. Sophia can you distill into a 3-line blurb + one slide? cc @Sophia :+1:

Sophia: Yep — I'll assemble a 1-slide summary and a 3-line blurb and drop into the GTN folder in ~2 hours. Will also include the exact monitoring gates and rollout playbook.

Leo: thanks team. small follow-up: can we capture hallucination-rate delta in the scorecard? even a relative number.

Mira: hallucination-rate change: INT8 +0.6% absolute, INT6 +1.8% (on the hallucination detector we run). I'll add that to the final slide.

Raj: ack on kernel/deploy timeline. I'll queue a build for a limited canary cluster for INT6 if you want to test warmup settings there.

Sophia: prefer to hold INT6 wider canary until we have product sign-off. For now I'll push INT8 canary plan.

Jules: perfect. if anyone sees a regression >1.5% on core slice during canary ping me and eng-ml oncall.

Sophia: noted. will post final blurb + slide here when ready.

Leo: :thumbsup:

Mira: ack

Benchbot: artifact checksum: sha256: a3b9... (full artifact available at link)

Sophia: thanks all — closing the loop once slide is in.
